Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks — this all makes sense. Quick answers to your questions and some details to help the network scoping call: 

1) VPC peering vs PrivateLink
- We support both on AWS. VPC peering is straightforward and low-latency; recommended for your use-case. PrivateLink is an alternative if you need to avoid route table changes. Either works; we’ll confirm the config on the call.

2) Static Egress IPs / NAT
- For VPC peering we typically route traffic over the peering connection (no public egress required for application traffic between your VPC and Redwood).
- For calls that originate from our infra to third-party services (if applicable), we can provision fixed NAT EIPs for outbound traffic — we’ll document the public IPs if you need them for allowlisting.

3) Ports & health checks
- Our checklist uses TLS on 443 for API traffic. Health checks use TCP/443 and occasional ICMP for tunnel validation. See attachment for the full port list.

4) Audit & logs
- Connection-level logs and session metadata are available in our Private control plane and can be exported to your S3/CloudWatch per the onboarding playbook. We’ll include the config pointers.

Attached: updated network_diagram.drawio (added peering example) and the network checklist (same PDF) for your network team.

Proposed technical next step: 30–45m call with Bob and our network engineer Sean to confirm CIDRs and routes. Sean — are you available Tue 11/17 10am PT? If not, Wed 11/18 14:00 PT works too.

Action items:
- Bob: share VPC CIDR(s) and route table ACLs prior to the call.
- Marissa: schedule invite and share runbook link.
- Sean: review peering requirements and prepare notes on egress IP provisioning.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Marissa
